requirements.subject: ent:value-parameter
requirements.canonical: A value of any basic type, any user-defined type, the address type, a component type, a port type, the timer type or the default type MAY be passed as a value parameter.
requirements.original: Values of all basic and user-defined types, address, component, port and timer types, and the default type can be passed as value parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:value-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal value parameter has the syntax [ ( `in` | `inout` | `out` ) ] [ ( `@lazy` | `@fuzzy` ) [ `@deterministic` ] ] TypeOrNestedTypeDef ValueParIdentifier [ ArrayDef ] [ ":=" ( Expression | "-" ) ].
requirements.original:
[ ( in | inout | out ) ] [ ( @lazy | @fuzzy ) [@deterministic] ] 
  TypeOrNestedTypeDef ValueParIdentifier [ArrayDef] [ ":=" ( Expression | "-" ) ]

requirements.subject: ent:value-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal value parameter CAN be used within the parameterized object in the same way as a value, e.g. in expressions.
requirements.original: Value formal parameters can be used within the parameterized object the same way as values, for example in expressions.

requirements.subject: ent:value-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal value parameter MAY be an in, inout or out parameter.
requirements.original: Value formal parameters may be in, inout or out parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:value-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal value parameter without a parameterization keyword IS an in parameter.
requirements.original: The default for value formal parameters is in parameterization which may optionally be denoted by the keyword in.

requirements.subject: ent:in-keyword
requirements.canonical: The in parameterization of a formal value parameter MAY optionally be denoted by the keyword `in`.
requirements.original: The default for value formal parameters is in parameterization which may optionally be denoted by the keyword in.

requirements.subject: ent:value-parameter
requirements.canonical: An inout or out formal value parameter SHALL be specified by the keyword `inout` or `out` respectively.
requirements.original: Using of inout or out kind of parameterization shall be specified by the keywords inout or out respectively.

requirements.subject: ent:in-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal in value parameter MAY have a default value, given by an expression assigned to the parameter.
requirements.original: In parameters may have a default value, which is given by an expression assigned to the parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:modified-template
requirements.canonical: A formal value parameter of a modified template MAY inherit the default value of the corresponding parameter of its parent template.
requirements.original: Formal parameters of modified templates may inherit the default values from the corresponding parameters of their parent templates; this shall explicitly be denoted by using a dash (don't change) symbol at the place of the modified template parameters' default value.

requirements.subject: ent:dash-symbol
requirements.canonical: Inheritance of a default value by a formal parameter of a modified template SHALL be denoted explicitly by the dash (don't change) symbol in place of the default value.
requirements.original: Formal parameters of modified templates may inherit the default values from the corresponding parameters of their parent templates; this shall explicitly be denoted by using a dash (don't change) symbol at the place of the modified template parameters' default value.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.condition: a function is used to initialize the default value
requirements.canonical: If a function is used for the initialization of a default value of an in parameter, side effects SHOULD be avoided during the evaluation of the default value.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: If functions are used for the initialization of default values of in parameters, it is strongly advised to avoid side effects during the evaluation of default values.

requirements.subject: ent:side-effect
requirements.canonical: A side effect during the evaluation of a default value CAN cause non-deterministic test executions.
requirements.original: Side effects may cause non-deterministic test executions.

requirements.subject: ent:side-effect
requirements.canonical: A side effect during the evaluation of a default value CAN be avoided, e.g. by adhering to the rules of clause 16.1.4.
requirements.original: They can be avoided, e.g. by adhering to the rules defined in clause 16.1.4.

requirements.subject: ent:module
requirements.canonical: A module supports static value parameterization to support test suite parameters.
requirements.original: the language element module allows static value parameterization to support test suite parameters, i.e. this parameterization may or may not be resolvable at compile-time but shall be resolved by the commencement of runtime (i.e. static at runtime).

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: The value of a module parameter MAY be unresolvable at compile-time.
requirements.original: the language element module allows static value parameterization to support test suite parameters, i.e. this parameterization may or may not be resolvable at compile-time but shall be resolved by the commencement of runtime (i.e. static at runtime).

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: The value of a module parameter SHALL be resolved by the commencement of runtime.
requirements.original: the language element module allows static value parameterization to support test suite parameters, i.e. this parameterization may or may not be resolvable at compile-time but shall be resolved by the commencement of runtime (i.e. static at runtime).

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: At runtime, a module parameter value IS globally visible.
requirements.original: This means that, at runtime, module parameter values are globally visible but not changeable (see more details in clause 8.2);

requirements.subject: ent:module-parameter
requirements.canonical: At runtime, a module parameter value SHALL NOT be changed.
requirements.original: This means that, at runtime, module parameter values are globally visible but not changeable (see more details in clause 8.2);

requirements.subject: ent:language-element
requirements.canonical: A template, testcase, altstep or function supports dynamic value parameterization.
requirements.original: the language elements template, testcase, `altstep and function support dynamic value` parameterization (i.e. this parameterization shall be resolved at runtime).

requirements.subject: ent:language-element
requirements.canonical: The dynamic value parameterization of a template, testcase, altstep or function SHALL be resolved at runtime.
requirements.original: the language elements template, testcase, `altstep and function support dynamic value` parameterization (i.e. this parameterization shall be resolved at runtime).

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.canonical: A component reference or a default reference IS handled as a value parameter.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: Component and default references are also handled as value parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.canonical: For a formal parameter receiving a component reference, the corresponding component type IS the type of the formal parameter.
requirements.original: In the case of component references, the corresponding component type is the type of the formal parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:default-reference
requirements.canonical: For a formal parameter receiving a default reference, the type `default` IS the type of the formal parameter.
requirements.original: In the case of default references the TTCN-3 type default is the type of the formal parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:language-element
requirements.canonical: A `const`, `var`, `timer`, `control`, `record of`, `set of`, `enumerated`, `port`, `component` or subtype definition, a `group` or an `import` SHALL NOT be parameterized.
requirements.original: a) Language elements which cannot be parameterized are: const, var, `timer, control,` `record` `of,` `set` `of, enumerated, port, component` and subtype definitions, group and import.

ambiguity.issue: The list names record of, set of and enumerated but not record, set or union type definitions, while clause 5.4.1.0 mentions structured types as parameterizable and table 2 lists none. Chosen reading: the listed elements are not parameterizable; the list says nothing about other type definitions.
readings: Only the listed language elements SHALL NOT be parameterized; record, set and union type definitions MAY be parameterized.
No type definition SHALL be parameterized; the list is only illustrative and table 2 is exhaustive.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.canonical: A formal value parameter of a template SHALL be an in parameter.
requirements.original: b) Formal value parameters of templates, and of altsteps activated as defaults (see clause 20.5.2) shall always be in parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: A formal value parameter of an altstep activated as a default SHALL be an in parameter.
requirements.original: b) Formal value parameters of templates, and of altsteps activated as defaults (see clause 20.5.2) shall always be in parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.canonical: A default value SHALL be provided only for a formal in parameter.
requirements.original: d) Default values can be provided for in parameters only.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.canonical: The expression of the default value of a formal parameter SHALL be compatible with the type of the parameter.
requirements.original: e) The expression of formal parameter's default value has to be compatible with the type of the parameter.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.canonical: The expression of the default value of a formal parameter MAY be any expression that is well-defined at the beginning of the scope of the parameterized entity.
requirements.original: The expression may be any expression that is well-defined at the beginning of the scope of the parameterized entity, but shall not refer to other parameters of the same parameter list.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.canonical: The expression of the default value of a formal parameter SHALL NOT refer to other parameters of the same parameter list.
requirements.original: The expression may be any expression that is well-defined at the beginning of the scope of the parameterized entity, but shall not refer to other parameters of the same parameter list.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.canonical: The default value of a component type formal parameter SHALL be one of the special values `null`, `mtc`, `self` or `system`.
requirements.original: f) Default values of component type formal parameters shall be one of the special values null, mtc, self, or system.

requirements.subject: ent:default-value
requirements.canonical: The default value of a port type, timer type or default type formal parameter SHALL be the special value `null`.
requirements.original: g) Default values of port, timer or default type formal parameters shall be the special value null.

requirements.subject: ent:dash-symbol
requirements.canonical: The dash (don't change) symbol SHALL be used only with formal parameters of modified templates.
requirements.original: h) The dash (don't change) symbol shall be used with formal parameters of modified templates only (see also clause 15.5).

requirements.subject: ent:value-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal value parameter of a template SHALL comply with the restrictions specified in clause 15.0.
requirements.original: i) For formal value parameters of templates the restrictions specified in clause 15.0 shall apply.

requirements.subject: ent:value-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal value parameter declared `@lazy` or `@fuzzy` SHALL be an in parameter.
requirements.original: j) Only in parameters can be declared lazy or fuzzy.

requirements.subject: ent:value-parameter
requirements.condition: the formal value parameter is referenced
requirements.canonical: When a formal value parameter is referenced (e.g. in assignments, expressions or template bodies), the rules for variables SHALL apply.
requirements.original: k) When parameters are referenced (e.g. in assignments, expressions, template bodies, etc.), the rules for variables shall apply.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: Only a function or altstep definition SHALL have formal parameters of a port, timer or default type or of a type containing a direct or indirect element or field of a port, default or timer type.
requirements.original: l) Only function and altstep definitions with the exception of functions or altsteps started as test component behaviour (see clause 21.3.2) may have formal parameters of a port, timer or default type or of a type that contains a direct or indirect element or field of a port, default or timer type.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: A function or altstep started as test component behaviour SHALL NOT have formal parameters of a port, timer or default type or of a type containing a direct or indirect element or field of a port, default or timer type.
requirements.original: l) Only function and altstep definitions with the exception of functions or altsteps started as test component behaviour (see clause 21.3.2) may have formal parameters of a port, timer or default type or of a type that contains a direct or indirect element or field of a port, default or timer type.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: Only a function, altstep or testcase definition SHALL have formal parameters of a component type or of a type containing a direct or indirect element or field of a component type.
requirements.original: m) Only function, altstep and testcase definitions may have formal parameters of a component type or of a type that contains a direct or indirect element or field of a component type.

requirements.subject: ent:deterministic-modifier
requirements.condition: the lazy or fuzzy value parameter is used in a deterministic context
requirements.canonical: If a lazy or fuzzy formal value parameter is used in a deterministic context (during the evaluation of a snapshot or the initialization of global non-fuzzy templates), it SHALL be declared `@deterministic`.
requirements.original: n) If a lazy or fuzzy value parameter is used in deterministic contexts (i.e. during the evaluation of a snapshot or initialization of global non-fuzzy templates), it shall be declared @deterministic.

non_requirement.reason: introductory sentence for the list of value parameterization rules (5.4.1.1-s013..s015)
pointer to clause 8.2 for restrictions on module parameters
